description:
AI can build almost anything you ask it to, which makes a harder question unavoidable: what's actually worth building? In this GitHub Universe 2026 conversation, Sue Black of Durham University and Kent C. Dodds of kody.codes make the case for building software deliberately rather than reflexively. This session explores what responsible software looks like and takes a deeper dive into the daily reality of shipping, choosing developer tools, and maintaining what is already built. You'll leave with a sharper set of questions to bring to your own work, along with a clearer sense of when development speed is worth it and when it isn't. 

Speakers: 

Kent C. Dodds, Product Engineer, kody.codes 
Sue Black, Professor of Computer Science and Technology Evangelist, Durham University

description:
In this episode of The GitHub Podcast, Andrea Griffiths and GPS are joined by the co-authors of the annual State of Commercial Open Source 2026 report: Matt Lavergne, a partner at VC firm Serena, and Sam Boysel, a data scientist with the Linux Foundation. Matt and Sam walk through what years of venture capital data on open source startups actually show: commercial open source companies raise money faster, close bigger rounds, and exit at significantly higher valuations than closed-source peers. They dig into which community and criticality signals actually matter instead, why the fear that “money ruins open source communities” mostly doesn’t hold up in the data, and how founders can build a business on top of an existing project without alienating maintainers, including real examples like pyannoteAI and MotherDuck. Finally, they share why open source founders turned out to be surprisingly optimistic about AI’s impact on their businesses.

title: Why GitHub stars don't pay the bills: inside commercial open source | S02E07 | The GitHub Podcast

Can you use GitHub Copilot to customize physical 3D prints? After printing a standard DJI microphone stand, we turned to the GitHub Copilot app to see if an AI prompt could modify the 3D model directly instead of relying on manual CAD software. The result embedded clean GitHub platform icons across the entire handle, creating a custom textured grip in minutes. It turns out developer AI tools can handle creative physical projects in ways you might not expect. What is the most unexpected or unusual project you have tackled with GitHub Copilot? Let us know in the comments below.
